title: Purchasing
section: What to buy and purchase orders
summary: The top of Purchasing: the way into What to buy, drafting all orders in one press, how each supplier delivers, and the list of purchase orders with their buttons (draft, approve, send, close, cancel).

parts.name: Heading and explanation
parts.shows: The heading Purchasing, the place switch (if the café has more than one place), and a short note: "Receive what a supplier delivers, each line as the invoice gives it. Freight and other costs are shared over the lines, and a price more than 25% away from what the item costs now is asked about first. The supplier's bill goes on Vendors."

controls.label: Stock at
controls.does: Chooses which of the café's places this device works for. The page reloads for that place. A delivery with no order, a new order and a return not named against a delivery are recorded for this place.
controls.rules: Shown only when the café has two or more places. The choice is kept on this device for a year.
controls.after: Nothing is recorded; only where the next records go.

controls.label: Vendors
controls.does: Opens Vendors, where the supplier's bill is recorded and paid.

controls.label: How it is booked
controls.does: Opens a note: receiving brings stock in at its landed cost and posts Dr 1200 Inventory / Cr 2050 Goods received not invoiced; the bill on Vendors clears 2050 and raises the payable, so nothing is counted twice.

parts.name: What to buy card
parts.shows: "What to buy": each item's stock, use and orders, and so how much to order and from whom, with why. Below it, for suppliers in use, a fold-out "How each supplier delivers".

controls.label: Open What to buy
controls.does: Opens the What to buy list for this place.

controls.label: Draft the orders now
controls.does: In one press, makes a draft purchase order for each supplier from everything What to buy says is to order and has a supplier and a price, in the packs suggested, plus the items that supplier would top up (items with enough, but less than halfway to their level). The button says "Drafting…" while it works. It then lists each draft ("Order {no} · supplier · total", each a link to the order), or says there is nothing to order, and names items that are to order but have no supplier or price.
controls.rules: Each draft is expected on today plus the days the supplier's deliveries take. Items already in a draft count as coming, so pressing again does not order them twice.
controls.who: Only those who may create orders (owner, general manager, branch manager, purchasing).
controls.after: Draft orders appear in the list below and on Approvals. Nothing happens to stock, money or the books until an order is approved, sent and received. Each supplier's pack and price for the item is remembered.

controls.label: How each supplier delivers
controls.does: Opens one line per supplier in use: how many days its deliveries take and how often it delivers, and where each number comes from.
controls.rules: Days a delivery takes: learnt once 3 or more orders sent in the last six months have had a delivery ("usually {n} day(s), later {late} time(s) in {orders} orders" or "usually {n} day(s), never later in {orders} orders"); else the days set on the supplier ("{n} day(s), as set (too few orders sent yet to learn it)"); else the café's own ("{n} day(s), the café's own (none set, too few orders to learn it)"). How often: set on the supplier ("delivers every {n} day(s)"), else learnt from 3 months of deliveries ("its deliveries come every {n} day(s) or so"), else "how often it delivers is not set yet (a week is assumed)".

parts.name: Purchase orders
parts.shows: A table of orders: No. (a link to the order's own page), Supplier, Expected, What has come (each line as received/ordered in its pack), Total, Stage (Draft, Approved, Sent, Partly received, Received, Closed, Cancelled; with "Approved by {name}" and any close or cancel reason), and the row's buttons. Above it, a note saying how orders move; for someone who approves it adds "yours is {limit}".

controls.label: New order
controls.does: Opens the order form ("A new order") above the table.
controls.rules: Hidden while a form is already open.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager, purchasing.

controls.label: Supplier
controls.does: In the order form: the supplier the order is for ("Choose…" first).
controls.rules: Required. Only suppliers in use are listed.

controls.label: Expected
controls.does: In the order form: the day the delivery is expected.
controls.rules: Optional date.

controls.label: Note for the supplier
controls.does: In the order form: a note printed on the order.
controls.rules: Optional, up to 300 letters.

controls.label: Item
controls.does: Each line's stock item ("Choose…" first). Choosing it sets the unit to the item's base unit.
controls.rules: Required on every line. An item may be on an order only once.

controls.label: Quantity
controls.does: How many of the unit are ordered.
controls.rules: More than zero. Arabic and Kurdish digits are accepted.

controls.label: Unit
controls.does: The item's base unit or one of its packs.
controls.rules: Enabled once an item is chosen.

controls.label: Price per unit
controls.does: The agreed price of one of the unit. The Amount column shows quantity × price, rounded to the dinar.
controls.rules: Required; zero or more.

controls.label: Remove the line (×)
controls.does: Takes the line off the form.
controls.rules: Shown only when there are two or more lines.

controls.label: Add a line
controls.does: Adds an empty line. The Total under the lines adds them up.
controls.rules: At most 100 lines on an order.

controls.label: Save the draft
controls.does: Saves the order as a draft ("Saving…" while it works) and closes the form with "Order {no} saved as a draft: {total}. A manager approves it next."
controls.rules: Enabled only when a supplier is chosen and every line has an item, a quantity above zero and a price.
controls.after: A draft order exists (it shows on Approvals and counts as "in draft" on What to buy). No stock or money moves. On the audit trail.

controls.label: Back
controls.does: Closes the order form without saving.

controls.label: Change
controls.does: Opens the order in the form to change its supplier, date, note or lines. For an approved order the form says "Order {no}: changed, it is a draft again and is approved again".
controls.rules: Only for a Draft or Approved order. A sent order cannot be changed.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager, purchasing.
controls.after: Saving an approved order makes it a draft again: it must be approved again.

controls.label: Approve
controls.does: Approves the draft: "Order {no} approved."
controls.rules: Only for a draft whose total is within your approval limit. Over it, the row says "Over your limit: the owner or the general manager approves it" instead.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager.
controls.after: The order is Approved, can be printed and sent, and deliveries can be received against it. On the audit trail.

controls.label: Approve and send
controls.does: Approves the draft and marks it sent to the supplier in one tap: "Order {no} approved and marked as sent to the supplier."
controls.rules: Only for a draft within your limit, for someone who may both approve and create orders. If the approval works but the sending is refused, the order stays Approved and the error is shown.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager.
controls.after: The order is Sent. The sent date starts the count of how many days the supplier takes.

controls.label: Mark as sent
controls.does: Records that the supplier has the order: "Order {no} marked as sent to the supplier."
controls.rules: Only for an Approved order.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager, purchasing.
controls.after: The order is Sent. Its sent date is used to learn how many days the supplier takes.

controls.label: Close
controls.does: Opens a box and the buttons "Close the order" and "Keep it". The box asks "Why is the rest not coming?" (or "A note (optional)" when everything has come).
controls.rules: Only for an Approved or Sent order that has had at least one delivery. A reason is needed when not everything has come.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager, purchasing.
controls.after: "Order {no} closed." Nothing more is expected; What to buy no longer counts the rest as coming. No stock or money moves.

controls.label: Cancel
controls.does: Opens a box "Why cancel it?" and the buttons "Cancel the order" and "Keep it".
controls.rules: Only while nothing has come against the order and it is not already closed or cancelled. A reason is required.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager, purchasing.
controls.after: "Order {no} cancelled." The order stays listed as Cancelled with its reason. No stock or money moves.

controls.label: Keep it
controls.does: Closes the close/cancel box without doing anything.

controls.label: No. (order number)
controls.does: Opens the order's own page, to read or print it.

messages.text: Your previous submission may already have been saved. Checking…

messages.text: Still no answer. It may have been saved: press the same button again to check. It will not be recorded twice.

messages.do: Reload the page and do it again.

messages.do: Reload the page, check whether the first try was saved, then do it again if it was not.

messages.do: Reload the page and do it again under your own sign-in.

messages.text: You do not have permission to do this (needs {1})
messages.when: Your roles do not give the permission the database asks for (for example the role was changed while the page was open).
messages.do: Ask the owner to give you the permission, or ask someone who has it.

messages.text: Sign in to continue

messages.do: Sign in again and repeat the step.

messages.text: Finish signing in: type the code from your authenticator app

messages.text: Your session has ended. Sign in again.

messages.do: Sign in again and repeat the step.

messages.do: Tell the owner or whoever runs the system: the database update must be applied.

what_if.case: The supplier says part of the order will never come
what_if.do: Receive what came, then press Close on the order and type why the rest is not coming.

what_if.case: An order was approved with a wrong price
what_if.do: If it has not been sent: press Change, fix the price and save (it becomes a draft), then approve again. If it was sent: cancel it (if nothing came) and draft a new one, or receive at the real price and close it.

what_if.case: The order was made for the wrong supplier and nothing has come
what_if.do: Press Cancel, type why, and draft a new order.

what_if.case: A branch manager's order is over their limit
what_if.do: It waits for the owner or general manager, on Approvals or here.

tips: Draft the orders now is the fastest way: one press makes every supplier's draft; then Approve and send each.

parts.name: Add supplier
parts.shows: A small card to add a supplier without leaving Purchasing.

controls.label: Name
controls.does: The supplier's name.
controls.rules: Required, up to 120 letters. No two suppliers in use may share a name, whatever the capitals, spaces or punctuation.

controls.label: What they supply
controls.does: A short note of what they sell.
controls.rules: Optional, up to 120 letters.

controls.label: Phone
controls.does: Their phone.
controls.rules: Optional, up to 40 letters.

controls.label: Add
controls.does: Adds the supplier ("…" while it works) and says "Supplier added." The boxes empty.
controls.rules: Enabled once a name is typed.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager, purchasing.
controls.after: The supplier appears in every supplier list (here, Vendors, What to buy). On the audit trail.

parts.name: Receive stock (goods receipt)
parts.shows: The delivery form. Under each line, the line's cost (quantity × price = total, what a base unit costs at this price, and what the item costs now), and, against an order, how the line differs from the order. At the bottom the goods value ("Goods {value}").

controls.label: Supplier
controls.does: Who delivered. Changing it to another supplier clears a chosen order of a different supplier.
controls.rules: Required; suppliers in use only. The first is chosen at the start.

controls.label: Freight (IQD)
controls.does: Delivery cost on the invoice, shared over the lines by value.
controls.rules: Optional, zero or more.
controls.after: Raises each line's landed cost.

controls.label: Other landed costs
controls.does: Other costs of bringing the goods in (customs, loading), shared over the lines by value.
controls.rules: Optional, zero or more.
controls.after: Raises each line's landed cost.

controls.label: Rebate (−)
controls.does: A discount off the whole invoice, taken off the lines by value.
controls.rules: Optional, zero or more; may not be more than a line's value.
controls.after: Lowers each line's landed cost.

controls.label: Against a purchase order
controls.does: "No order", or an open order written "Order {no}: {supplier} ({stage})". Choosing an order sets the supplier and fills the lines with what is still to come, in the order's units, at the order's prices.
controls.rules: Shown only when there are open (approved or sent) orders. Lists the chosen supplier's orders, or all open orders when that supplier has none.

controls.label: Item
controls.does: The line's item. The first choice, "+ New item (not in Inventory yet)…", opens a small form to add the item here.
controls.rules: The new-item choice is offered to the owner, general manager, branch manager and purchasing.

controls.label: Quantity
controls.does: How many of the unit came.
controls.rules: More than zero. A line with an empty quantity is left out.

controls.label: Unit
controls.does: The item's base unit or one of its packs, written with what it holds, e.g. "Carton (12 l)".

controls.label: Price per {unit} (IQD)
controls.does: The price of one of the chosen unit, exactly as the invoice gives it.
controls.rules: Required, zero or more. If the cost per base unit is more than 25% above or below what the item costs now, the cost line turns orange: "{pct}% above: check it" / "{pct}% below: check it".

controls.label: Remove line (×)
controls.does: Takes the line off.
controls.rules: Disabled when there is only one line.

controls.label: + Add line
controls.does: Adds a line.

controls.label: Note (delivery note number, etc.)
controls.does: A note kept with the receipt.
controls.rules: Optional, up to 300 letters.

controls.label: Receive goods
controls.does: Sends the delivery ("Receiving…" while it works). If a price is far from the cost now, or more is coming than is still on the order, a warning card asks first instead of receiving.
controls.rules: Disabled while a new item is being added ("Add the new item first, or choose one from the list.") or while the warning card is open.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager, purchasing.
controls.after: Stock goes up at this place at each line's landed cost, and each item's average cost changes. The books get Dr 1200 Inventory / Cr 2050 Goods received not invoiced. The receipt gets a number and shows as "Awaiting bill" (its bill is recorded on Vendors). Against an order, the order shows what has come (Partly received or Received). A confirmed price or extra quantity is written on the audit trail.

controls.label: The price is right: receive it / It is right: receive it
controls.does: In the warning card: receives the delivery as it is, confirming the price or the extra quantity.
controls.after: As Receive goods, and your confirmation goes on the audit trail.

controls.label: Let me correct it
controls.does: Closes the warning card so the line can be fixed.

controls.label: A new stock item (form on the line)
controls.does: Name (English), الاسم (Arabic), ناو (Kurdish), Type, Measured in, Base unit, The pack it is bought in (optional) and Holds, Reorder level, a tick "Goes back on the shelf when a sale is refunded (sealed goods only)", then "Add the item" (or "It is a different item: add it" when a look-alike name exists) and Cancel. Items with a similar name are shown with "Use it" and "Open it".
controls.rules: Opening stock is not offered here: the item's stock comes in with this delivery.
controls.after: The item is added to Inventory and the line uses it: "Added “{name}” to Inventory: its stock comes in with this delivery."

parts.shows: No. (with a paperclip to its documents), When (the day it came; if that differs from when it was entered, hovering shows "Entered {when}"), Supplier (or the old note), Lines, Goods, Landed extras, Into stock, Bill. The owner posts its journal from Reports → Do the books tie?"), Before controls (hover: "Received before the controls; its journal has been reversed"). Under a corrected delivery, a line per correction: "Correction {no} · when · who · what changed · “reason” · stock {stock}, owed for it {grni}, price variance {variance} (journal {journal})" or "nothing to post". Managers see a note on correcting above the table.

controls.rules: As Correct.

After Show what it would do: a table per item (On the delivery before → after, In stock before → after (red below zero), Stock value, Owed for it (2050), Price variance (5050)) and the totals "Stock {stock} · owed for it {grni} · price variance {variance}".

parts.name: Heading
parts.shows: "What to buy", the place switch, a line "{place} · {day} · use judged over the last {days} days" (up to 28), and a one-line explanation with "How this works" to open the rest: an item is to order when what it has on hand, on order and in draft orders is below its reorder level (its own, set on the item, or its use for the days a delivery takes, and a day more); it is ordered up to its par level (or the reorder level and a week of use) in whole packs, from its usual supplier or the one its last delivery came from. With the newer rules it also says what is thrown away is not counted as use, each day is judged by its weekday, today's plan is added, and an item that keeps only a few days is ordered up to no more than those days' use.

parts.name: One card per supplier (the items to order)
parts.shows: The items to order, and any added by hand or topped up, grouped by supplier ("No supplier yet" last). Each card's top line: the supplier, "Delivers in {n} day(s)" (or "Delivers in the café's {n} day(s)", or "Choose a supplier for each line"), and "{n} ticked · {total}". Columns: tick, Item (a link to the item's page; "Added by hand" or "Topped up with this order" under it when it is not to order on its own), Why, Quantity, Pack, Price of a pack, Amount, Supplier. Why gives what it has and what to order first, e.g. "2,000 ml on hand." and in bold "5 × Carton (12,000 ml), rounded up to whole packs."; then "How it was worked out" opens the rest: its reorder level and where it comes from (set on the item; its use; today's plan), the days a delivery takes (learnt, set on the supplier or the café's), days it came late, a safety stock, waste not counted as use, the suggested level beside one set by hand, and what it is ordered up to (par level, the most it holds, a week of use, until the delivery after this one). Below: where the supplier and price come from ("Its usual supplier.", "The supplier of its last delivery.", "{price} a pack, agreed {day}.", "{price} a pack, as delivered {day}.", "{price} a pack, from what it costs now: check it with the supplier.", "No price yet: enter one.", "{supplier} sells it {pct} cheaper: {price} a pack.") and the open orders it is on ("Order {no}: {qty}", links).

get_there: Menu → Spending → Vendors (in the main menu for the owner, general manager, accountant and purchasing; under More for the branch manager and the auditor). Also from Find anything (a supplier's name opens Vendors on that supplier), and from links on Purchasing. Choose the supplier, then the tab Bills & payments.
before: For a bill for goods: the delivery has been received on Purchasing and is not billed yet.
To pay from the till: the drawer is open at this device's place. To pay from the safe: the safe holds enough in the books.

parts.name: Record a bill
parts.shows: "The supplier's invoice — raises what you owe". Hints under the form: the café's own number explained; "Type the amount the supplier's invoice says. It is checked against the {amount} the receipt recorded."; and when the amount differs from the receipt: "The bill is {amount} more than the receipt recorded; the difference goes to 5050 Purchase price variance." (or "less").

controls.label: For goods received
controls.does: The bill is for a delivery.
controls.rules: Disabled with "(no unbilled receipts)" when this supplier has no delivery awaiting a bill.

controls.label: For a service or asset (rent, repairs, equipment…)
controls.does: The bill is charged straight to an account.

controls.label: Goods receipt
controls.does: The delivery the bill is for: "Receipt {no} · date · value", or "Before controls · {note}" for old deliveries whose supplier was not recorded.
controls.rules: This supplier's deliveries awaiting a bill, and old ones with no supplier.

controls.label: Charge to account
controls.does: The expense or asset account for a service bill.
controls.rules: Cash, bank, stock and other protected accounts are not offered.

controls.label: Invoice no.
controls.does: Starts with the café's own next number (for example SGC-2026-0001). Type the supplier's own invoice number over it if it has one.
controls.rules: Up to 60 letters. The same number from the same supplier can be entered only once. Do not type a number in the café's own pattern.

controls.label: Invoice date
controls.does: The bill's date.
controls.rules: Up to today; not before the delivery came.
controls.after: The bill is booked on this date.

controls.label: Amount (IQD)
controls.does: The total on the supplier's invoice. Type it from the invoice; it is not copied from the receipt.
controls.rules: More than zero.

controls.label: Terms
controls.does: Due now, Net 7 days, Net 15 days (default), Net 30 days.
controls.after: The due date is the invoice date plus the terms; used by the ageing cards.

controls.label: Record bill
controls.does: Records the bill ("Saving…").
controls.rules: Enabled when an amount and the receipt (or account) are chosen.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager, purchasing, accountant.
controls.after: For goods: clears Goods received not invoiced (Dr 2050) for what the receipt recorded, puts any difference to 5050 Purchase price variance, and raises Accounts payable (Cr 2000); the delivery shows Billed on Purchasing and can no longer be corrected. For a service: Dr the account / Cr 2000. The bill shows under Open bills and on the statement.

parts.name: Open bills
parts.shows: "{n} unpaid". Columns Invoice (with a paperclip to its documents), Dated, Due, Total, Outstanding, Status ("{n}d overdue" or "Current"). Bills are sorted most overdue first. "Nothing outstanding." when none.

controls.label: Paperclip
controls.does: Opens the bill's documents page (to keep a photo of the invoice).

controls.label: Cancel
controls.does: On a bill with nothing paid and no credit set against it: opens a reason box ("Why cancel {bill}?"), a date (Date of the cancellation), Confirm and Keep. Hover: "Entered in error — a duplicate or the wrong amount".
controls.rules: Reason required; date from the bill's date to today.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, accountant.
controls.after: The bill stays on record, marked cancelled on the statement; its journal is reversed on the date chosen; it is no longer owed; its delivery is Awaiting bill again (and can be corrected).

controls.label: Confirm
controls.does: Cancels the bill ("…" while it works).
controls.rules: Enabled once a reason is typed.

controls.label: Keep
controls.does: Closes the cancel boxes.

parts.name: Pay bill
parts.shows: Under Open bills, for those who may pay. Under the form, what the money source holds (see messages).

controls.label: Pay bill
controls.does: Choose the bill ("Choose an invoice…"); each is "{invoice} — {amount} outstanding". Choosing one fills the amount with what is outstanding.

controls.label: Amount (IQD)
controls.does: How much is paid now; can be less than outstanding (part payment).
controls.rules: More than zero, not more than outstanding.

controls.label: Paid from
controls.does: Choose…, The till (today's drawer), The safe, The bank, A card, The owner, personally.
controls.rules: Required.

controls.label: Record payment
controls.does: Records the payment ("Paying…").
controls.rules: Enabled when a bill, an amount and a source are chosen. From the till: the drawer must be open and hold enough. From the safe: the safe must hold enough in the books.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, accountant.
controls.after: Dr 2000 Accounts payable / Cr 1000 Cash in the till, 1005 Cash in the safe, 1020 Bank (bank or card) or 3000 Owner equity. From the till the cash leaves this device's drawer (the drawer's expected cash goes down). The bill's outstanding goes down; at zero it leaves Open bills. The payment shows on the statement.

what_if.do: Press Cancel on the second one (only possible while nothing is paid on it), type "entered twice", Confirm.

what_if.case: Paying half now and half later
what_if.do: Record payment with the half; the rest stays outstanding.

what_if.case: The owner paid the supplier from his own pocket
what_if.do: Paid from: The owner, personally. It is booked as money the owner put in.

parts.name: Credit notes
parts.shows: "What this supplier owes back: goods returned after their bill, a lower price agreed on a delivery, or other. Each is set against their bills; what is left waits for the next one." Table: No. (with a paperclip), Date, For (Goods returned / A lower price / Other, with "return {no}" or "delivery {no}" and the reason), Their note, Amount, Left.

controls.label: Paperclip
controls.does: Opens the credit's documents page (keep the supplier's credit note there).

controls.label: The number on their credit note (with Record it)
controls.does: For a return's credit still "Awaiting their note": type the number on the supplier's credit note and press Record it.
controls.rules: Up to 60 letters; a number used already for this supplier is refused.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager, purchasing, accountant (others see the badge "Awaiting their note").
controls.after: Only the number is recorded; nothing is posted again.

controls.label: Set it against
controls.does: On a credit with something left: chooses one of the supplier's unpaid bills ("Bill {no} ({owed} owed)"); the amount fills with the smaller of what is left and what is owed.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, accountant.

controls.label: Amount
controls.does: How much of the credit to set against the bill.
controls.rules: More than zero; not more than what is left or what the bill still owes.

controls.label: Set against it
controls.does: Sets the amount against the bill.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, accountant.
controls.after: The bill's outstanding goes down by that much (no cash moves); the credit's Left goes down. A bill with a credit set against it can no longer be cancelled.

parts.name: Record their credit note
parts.shows: A form for a credit the supplier gives that is not a return (a return makes its own credit on Purchasing). Under it: for a price, "The stock of that delivery still on the shelf is revalued; what was used since goes to the price variance (5050). It is set against the delivery's bill."; for other, "It comes off the account chosen, and is set against the bill chosen as far as it is owed."

controls.label: A lower price on a delivery that was billed
controls.does: The credit lowers the price of a billed delivery.
controls.rules: Disabled when the supplier has no billed delivery.

controls.label: Other: a service, an overcharge
controls.does: The credit comes off an account.

controls.label: The number on their credit note
controls.does: The supplier's credit note number.
controls.rules: Required, up to 60 letters; once per supplier.

controls.label: Amount (IQD)
controls.does: The credit's amount.
controls.rules: More than zero. For a price, not more than what the delivery is still worth.

controls.label: The delivery
controls.does: For a price: the billed delivery ("Delivery {no}").

controls.label: Against a bill
controls.does: For other: one of the supplier's unpaid bills, or "None: left on the account".

controls.label: Taken off the account
controls.does: For other: the account the credit lowers. With a service bill chosen, the first choice is "The bill's own ({code})".
controls.rules: Required unless the bill's own account is used. Cash, bank, stock and other protected accounts are not offered.

controls.label: What it is for
controls.does: The reason.
controls.rules: Required, up to 300 letters.

controls.label: Record the credit
controls.does: Records the credit ("Saving…").
controls.rules: Enabled when the number, the amount, the reason and the delivery (or account) are given.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager, purchasing, accountant.
controls.after: Lowers Accounts payable (Dr 2000). For a price: the part of that delivery's stock still on the shelf is lowered in value (Cr 1200) and the rest goes to 5050 price variance; it is set against the delivery's bill as far as it is owed. For other: Cr the account chosen, set against the bill chosen. Shown on the statement as a credit.

messages.text: {n} month(s)' share posted as an expense of its month.
messages.when: Release worked.

messages.text: Say why the prepaid expense is cancelled
messages.when: The reason is only spaces.
messages.do: Type a reason.

messages.text: Prepaid expense not found
messages.when: It no longer exists.
messages.do: Reload.

messages.text: That prepaid expense was cancelled already
messages.when: Cancelled meanwhile.
messages.do: Reload.

messages.text: Journal {1} has already been reversed
messages.when: Its journal was reversed by hand on Journals.
messages.do: Ask the accountant.

messages.text: Accounting period {1} is locked; post into an open period or reverse in the current one
messages.when: The step would write to the books in a month that has been locked (closed).
messages.do: Use a date in an open month, or ask the accountant or owner to unlock the month.

messages.text: Your previous submission may already have been saved. Checking…
messages.when: The app sent the form but no answer came back; it is sending it again by itself (up to three times), with the same key.
messages.do: Wait. It will not be recorded twice.

messages.text: Still no answer. It may have been saved: press the same button again to check. It will not be recorded twice.
messages.when: Three tries brought no answer (the connection is down or very slow).
messages.do: Check the connection, then press the same button again. The database recognises the same submission and does not record it twice.

messages.text: This screen sent no retry key: reload the page and try again
messages.when: The page is old or broken and sent the form without its one-time key.
messages.do: Reload the page and do it again.

messages.text: This retry does not match what was first sent: reload the page and check before doing it again
messages.when: A retry was sent with different values from the first try.
messages.do: Reload the page, check whether the first try was saved, then do it again if it was not.

messages.text: This was sent by someone else
messages.when: The same submission key was used by another person's sign-in (two people on one device).
messages.do: Reload the page and do it again under your own sign-in.

messages.text: You do not have permission to do this (needs {1})
messages.when: Your roles do not give the permission the database asks for (for example the role was changed while the page was open).
messages.do: Ask the owner to give you the permission, or ask someone who has it.

messages.text: Sign in to continue
messages.when: You are no longer signed in.
messages.do: Sign in again and repeat the step.

messages.text: Finish signing in: type the code from your authenticator app
messages.when: Your account uses two-step sign-in and the code step was not finished.
messages.do: Type the code from your authenticator app, then repeat the step.

messages.text: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
messages.when: Your sign-in ran out.
messages.do: Sign in again and repeat the step.

messages.text: The database is missing an update this screen needs (a migration has not been applied yet).
messages.when: The app was updated but the database was not.
messages.do: Tell the owner or whoever runs the system: the database update must be applied.
